Schiff Jabs Saylor
Schiff described Saylor’s remarks that the CLARITY Act’s failure marked a positive turning point for Bitcoin as "self-serving," which ended up being another catalyst for the rally.
“I’m sure he’d [Michael Saylor] have said the same thing had the Act been passed into law,” the longtime Bitcoin critic took a dig.
My thoughts on why the rejection of CLARITY marks a positive inflection point for Digital Assets, and why supportive rules and free markets should now accelerate innovation and growth.
Schiff also slammed the company’s decision to sell Bitcoin at lower prices and later acquire it at higher prices.
“It won’t be long before he’s selling at lower prices again,” the economist predicted.
Strategy didn’t return Benzinga’s request for comment.

During its last Bitcoin selling spree, Strategy sold 6,948 Bitcoin for approximately $431.8 million in net proceeds, or about $62,150 per Bitcoin. Now he's buying back some of what he sold for over $80K per Bitcoin. It won't be long before he's selling at lower prices again.
